correctness.rationale: The exact Runge–Kutta stability rational R(z)=(1+z/3)/(1−2z/3+z²/6) has fifth Taylor coefficient −1/108. At graph distance exactly five all generator matrix-power entries below degree five vanish, while the fifth is positive sum of positive weighted geodesic walks, proving a strict negative leading term. At large h, finite connected symmetric spectral calculus gives projection to the uniform constant vector, strictly positive. For n=2..6, the supplied exact certificate lists every one of 55 upper-triangular common-denominator polynomial numerators; independent SymPy reconstruction from L_n established nonnegative coefficients except one negative h^5 term in P_6 (0,5). Its exact factored rational numerator is h^5 q(h)/D(h), D positive on h≥0; Descartes and q(0)<0 isolate a unique positive root. Thus the all-step path boundary and exact P_6 recovery follow without extrapolating finite computations to unrestricted graphs.

Zappavigna–Colaneri–Kirkland–Shorten’s accessible primary work studies diagonal Padé discretizations, unlike this subdiagonal [1/2] Radau completed step. The quantitative sharp path threshold is the assessed addition, with historical equivalent numerical-analysis analyses as a residual risk.

value.rationale: Positivity is essential for graph heat/Markov simulation. The theorem identifies a counterintuitive graph-distance obstruction even at arbitrarily small positive timesteps, the first failing unit path and its exact quantitative recovery time. It is a motivated sharp boundary, not a routine instance of an arbitrary matrix calculation.

final_claim: For third-order two-stage Radau IIA completed graph heat steps, distance-five entries are negative for sufficiently small h on all positive weighted connected graphs, while all entries become positive for large h. Unit-edge path P_n preserves positivity for every step size iff n≤5. On P_6 only opposite endpoints fail for 0<h<τ, with τ=0.131359689579… unique positive root of h^5+35h^4+168h^3+216h²+60h−12.
limitations: Unweighted paths only for sharp n-boundary and τ; general weighted graphs only small/large time claims.
